title: Are you good at AI? Companies are now basing performance reviews on it
excerpt: Companies are scrambling to figure out how to grade employees' AI use in performance reviews.
content_html:
Are you good at AI? Your next raise may depend on it

Companies are scrambling to figure out how to grade employees' AI use

By Amanda Hoover

You're currently following this author! Want to unfollow? Unsubscribe via the link in your email.

2026-08-13T08:17:01.234Z

Read in app

Bosses everywhere are scrambling to figure out if and how to grade their employees' AI use.

At Gusto, a platform for human resources, managers slot workers into one of five AI archetypes during quarterly reviews. They may begin as "observers," those who aren't yet using AI on their own. "Integrators" have made AI part of their regular work day and see "better outcomes consistently" as a result. The most advanced are "amplifiers," who find new ways to use AI and share what they've learned with coworkers.

The intent is less to rule by the carrot or the stick, and more to standardize how the company implements an emerging technology, says Scott Helmes, Gusto's chief people officer. "We want to be able to have a coaching conversation," he tells me. The next step is to look more directly at the impact workers make with AI. "The introduction of this, I think, has really helped us have a consistent way to talk about AI fluency across the organization."

The employee AI grading rubric started with tokenmaxxing, but the backlash quickly arrived. Companies like Amazon and Uber tried leaderboards for tracking AI use, but have since pivoted away from maxing out AI. Duolingo walked back plans to evaluate AI use in employee performance reviews. Meta faces a lawsuit from laid-off workers alleging that the company used AI to rank workers' productivity, including how often they used AI tools, and then singled out lower performers for cuts without considering medical and parental leaves as reasons for lower usage. The company has denied the allegations.

Workplaces can't take macro leaps of AI adoption until they sort out what's happening on the micro level and individual workers' desks as they corral agents and chatbots. Attempts to suss out those who shun AI from the superusers has increasingly become part of performance reviews, but with many companies still looking to unearth AI's potential, that can leave workers clambering to meet expectations that managers haven't fully formed. "There's a lot of drive to push that responsibility onto frontline workers in a way that's not particularly fair," says Richard Landers, a professor of industrial-organizational psychology at the University of Minnesota. Some companies have made the false equivalence of rewarding AI use even if it doesn't achieve the goal of better work, he says. "You can't really reward AI performance because we don't really know what that even is yet, and it also looks very different for different jobs."

AI might be a box to check in your next performance review. But when success with the technology remains rare and subjective, it's an elusive category to ace.

Companies have largely dropped subscriptions and logins to AI systems onto workers and urged them to figure out how to best use them. The lack of training and brute force adoption has led to a deluge of workslop, security risks, and a confusing sprawl of sprawl workflows. Yet, managers increasingly want to evaluate how people use AI. General Assembly, the tech skills training provider, found in a recent survey of 500 business leaders in the US and UK that nearly half had incorporated AI into employee reviews, looking particularly at reports of AI tool usage, improvements to performance attributable to AI, and anecdotes about improved efficiency.

Much of that is subjective, and unlike past innovations where companies bought software for specific use cases and trained workers on it, there's an expectation at some companies that the workers lead.

Without strict quantitative benchmarks like tokens spent, lines of code generated, prompts written, and agents deployed, many evaluate workers' AI use by tracking that they're doing more of what they did before. Stefan Camilleri, vice president of engineering at the software company Typeform, says he asks his engineers: "Now that I've given you a new tool, how much faster are you doing it?" But speed alone doesn't cut it. "I'm expecting more ambitious output from fewer people." Shensi Ding, the cofounder and CEO of the AI software company Merge, says she reviews employees based on the quality of their AI use. For example, someone in accounting automated payment tracking and increased the team's productivity, which Ding saw as highly effective. The highest praise comes for those who have figured out a good use case and passed it along to their colleagues. "If you're teaching other people, then that's a level above what we would expect, and it's such a big impact and compounds over time in the business that people are really rewarded for that," Ding says.

For startups, there's pressure to do more with fewer people equipped with AI, but large companies are also now closely evaluating workers' AI use. Meta announced to employees late last year that it would add "AI driven impact" as a core part of their performance review process. Accenture reportedly began monitoring AI logins when considering workers for top-level promotions earlier this year. My colleague Hugh Langley reported earlier this year that non-technical employees at Google were told that AI use could show up in their performance reviews. The company says that managers can evaluate AI proficiency in reviews, but it's not a requirement.

Many companies are still in an experimental phase, focusing on how AI can add value rather than who uses the most. Lee Senderov, chief transformation officer at Travelport, a retail platform for travel agencies, says her company has built a dashboard for engineers that uses AI to analyze code and determine the tools used to write it. Managers can see if an engineer isn't using particular AI features, and then use those insights to have conversations about what particular workers do or don't understand, and how they're coding. AI, Senderov says, is case by case for different functions, and the mandatory push or rollout may not lend itself as well in some places as others. "We want this to happen organically and happen through inspiration," she says.

Across corporate America, the lack of clarity over what AI materially means for performance reviews has led evaluations to feel uneven and wonky. A July Harvard Business Review article called for reviews to focus not on output, but on how workers can evaluate the accuracy of AI and then use judgement to override errors, if a worker uses AI to increase the productivity of their team, and how well they adapt to new technology, policy changes, and workflows.

Many companies haven't standardized these changes. A January Deloitte report found that 84% of companies have not redesigned work to meet the capabilities of AI; the emphasis remains on educating workers and pushing them to experiment with AI, rather than altering workflows and career paths to match the tech changes. "Leaders are realizing that this usage conversation isn't having the impact that they were looking for," says Lori Moffatt, managing director of executive recruitment and company culture advisory firm Waterstone's Leadership and Culture Advisory Services. Anyone can prompt AI or find a task ripe for automation, fewer have found real problems that merit an AI solution. "AI is meant to be transformational. And yet managing it the ways that they're managing today is not creating the transformation that they're looking for."

Marc Cenedella, founder of the career site Ladders, says that while AI advances rapidly, people need more time to fully discover and stretch its technical feats into meaningful work. He encourages workers to experiment with AI, to fail — even if one day we look back and see these early efforts as "goofing around." "It kind of doesn't matter if it's useless or useful at this point," Cenedella says. If AI had obvious benefits, industries would streamline it. "If this was measurable, that would mean it's not an amazing technology."

Amanda Hoover is a senior correspondent at Business Insider covering the tech industry. She writes about the biggest tech companies and trends.

blocks.html_en: Without strict quantitative benchmarks like tokens spent, lines of code generated, prompts written, and agents deployed, many evaluate workers' AI use by tracking that they're doing more of what they did before. Stefan Camilleri, vice president of engineering at the software company Typeform, says he asks his engineers: "Now that I've given you a new tool, how much faster are you doing it?" But speed alone doesn't cut it. "I'm expecting more ambitious output from fewer people." Shensi Ding, the cofounder and CEO of the AI software company Merge, says she reviews employees based on the quality of their AI use. For example, someone in accounting automated payment tracking and increased the team's productivity, which Ding saw as highly effective. The highest praise comes for those who have figured out a good use case and passed it along to their colleagues. "If you're teaching other people, then that's a level above what we would expect, and it's such a big impact and compounds over time in the business that people are really rewarded for that," Ding says.

sentences.en: Without strict quantitative benchmarks like tokens spent, lines of code generated, prompts written, and agents deployed, many evaluate workers' AI use by tracking that they're doing more of what they did before.
sentences.zh: 如果没有严格的定量基准，例如花费的代币、生成的代码行、编写的提示和部署的代理，许多人通过跟踪他们所做的事情是否比以前做得更多来评估他们的人工智能使用情况。

sentences.en: Stefan Camilleri, vice president of engineering at the software company Typeform, says he asks his engineers: "Now that I've given you a new tool, how much faster are you doing it?"
sentences.zh: 软件公司 Typeform 的工程副总裁 Stefan Camilleri 说，他问工程师：“既然我给了你们一个新工具，你们的速度要快多少？”

sentences.en: But speed alone doesn't cut it.
sentences.zh: 但仅靠速度并不能解决问题。

sentences.en: "I'm expecting more ambitious output from fewer people."
sentences.zh: “我期待更少的人能做出更雄心勃勃的成果。”

sentences.en: Shensi Ding, the cofounder and CEO of the AI software company Merge, says she reviews employees based on the quality of their AI use.
sentences.zh: 人工智能软件公司 Merge 的联合创始人兼首席执行官丁申思表示，她根据员工使用人工智能的质量来评估他们。

sentences.en: For example, someone in accounting automated payment tracking and increased the team's productivity, which Ding saw as highly effective.
sentences.zh: 例如，会计人员自动跟踪付款并提高了团队的生产力，丁认为这非常有效。

sentences.en: The highest praise comes for those who have figured out a good use case and passed it along to their colleagues.
sentences.zh: 最高的赞扬来自于那些找到了一个好的用例并将其传递给同事的人。

sentences.en: "If you're teaching other people, then that's a level above what we would expect, and it's such a big impact and compounds over time in the business that people are really rewarded for that," Ding says.
sentences.zh: 丁说：“如果你在教其他人，那么这会超出我们的预期水平，而且随着时间的推移，它会对行业产生巨大的影响和复合，人们会因此而真正得到回报。”

blocks.html_en: For startups, there's pressure to do more with fewer people equipped with AI, but large companies are also now closely evaluating workers' AI use. Meta announced to employees late last year that it would add "AI driven impact" as a core part of their performance review process. Accenture reportedly began monitoring AI logins when considering workers for top-level promotions earlier this year. My colleague Hugh Langley reported earlier this year that non-technical employees at Google were told that AI use could show up in their performance reviews. The company says that managers can evaluate AI proficiency in reviews, but it's not a requirement.

sentences.en: For startups, there's pressure to do more with fewer people equipped with AI, but large companies are also now closely evaluating workers' AI use.
sentences.zh: 对于初创公司来说，他们面临着用更少的人工智能人员做更多事情的压力，但大公司现在也在密切评估员工对人工智能的使用情况。

sentences.en: Meta announced to employees late last year that it would add "AI driven impact" as a core part of their performance review process.
sentences.zh: Meta 去年年底向员工宣布，它将添加“人工智能驱动的影响”作为其绩效评估流程的核心部分。

sentences.en: Accenture reportedly began monitoring AI logins when considering workers for top-level promotions earlier this year.
sentences.zh: 据报道，埃森哲今年早些时候在考虑员工进行高层晋升时开始监控人工智能登录。

sentences.en: My colleague Hugh Langley reported earlier this year that non-technical employees at Google were told that AI use could show up in their performance reviews.
sentences.zh: 我的同事休·兰利 (Hugh Langley) 今年早些时候报告称，谷歌的非技术员工被告知人工智能的使用可能会出现在他们的绩效评估中。

sentences.en: The company says that managers can evaluate AI proficiency in reviews, but it's not a requirement.
sentences.zh: 该公司表示，经理可以在评审中评估人工智能的熟练程度，但这不是必需的。

blocks.html_en: Many companies are still in an experimental phase, focusing on how AI can add value rather than who uses the most. Lee Senderov, chief transformation officer at Travelport, a retail platform for travel agencies, says her company has built a dashboard for engineers that uses AI to analyze code and determine the tools used to write it. Managers can see if an engineer isn't using particular AI features, and then use those insights to have conversations about what particular workers do or don't understand, and how they're coding. AI, Senderov says, is case by case for different functions, and the mandatory push or rollout may not lend itself as well in some places as others. "We want this to happen organically and happen through inspiration," she says.

sentences.en: Many companies are still in an experimental phase, focusing on how AI can add value rather than who uses the most.
sentences.zh: 许多公司仍处于试验阶段，关注人工智能如何增加价值，而不是谁使用最多。

sentences.en: Lee Senderov, chief transformation officer at Travelport, a retail platform for travel agencies, says her company has built a dashboard for engineers that uses AI to analyze code and determine the tools used to write it.
sentences.zh: 旅行社零售平台 Travelport 的首席转型官 Lee Senderov 表示，她的公司为工程师构建了一个仪表板，使用人工智能来分析代码并确定用于编写代码的工具。

sentences.en: Managers can see if an engineer isn't using particular AI features, and then use those insights to have conversations about what particular workers do or don't understand, and how they're coding.
sentences.zh: 经理可以了解工程师是否没有使用特定的人工智能功能，然后利用这些见解就特定员工理解或不理解的内容以及他们如何编码进行对话。

sentences.en: AI, Senderov says, is case by case for different functions, and the mandatory push or rollout may not lend itself as well in some places as others.
sentences.zh: 森德罗夫表示，人工智能针对不同的功能，是根据具体情况而定的，强制推动或推出可能并不适合某些地方。

sentences.en: "We want this to happen organically and happen through inspiration," she says.
sentences.zh: “我们希望这一切能够通过灵感有机地发生，”她说。

blocks.html_en: Across corporate America, the lack of clarity over what AI materially means for performance reviews has led evaluations to feel uneven and wonky. A July Harvard Business Review article called for reviews to focus not on output, but on how workers can evaluate the accuracy of AI and then use judgement to override errors, if a worker uses AI to increase the productivity of their team, and how well they adapt to new technology, policy changes, and workflows.

sentences.en: Across corporate America, the lack of clarity over what AI materially means for performance reviews has led evaluations to feel uneven and wonky.
sentences.zh: 在整个美国企业界，人工智能对绩效评估的实质意义缺乏明确性，导致评估感觉不平衡和不稳定。

sentences.en: A July Harvard Business Review article called for reviews to focus not on output, but on how workers can evaluate the accuracy of AI and then use judgement to override errors, if a worker uses AI to increase the productivity of their team, and how well they adapt to new technology, policy changes, and workflows.
sentences.zh: 《哈佛商业评论》7 月份的一篇文章呼吁审查不要关注产出，而应该关注员工如何评估人工智能的准确性，然后利用判断来覆盖错误，如果员工使用人工智能来提高团队的生产力，以及他们对新技术、政策变化和工作流程的适应程度如何。

blocks.html_en: Many companies haven't standardized these changes. A January Deloitte report found that 84% of companies have not redesigned work to meet the capabilities of AI; the emphasis remains on educating workers and pushing them to experiment with AI, rather than altering workflows and career paths to match the tech changes. "Leaders are realizing that this usage conversation isn't having the impact that they were looking for," says Lori Moffatt, managing director of executive recruitment and company culture advisory firm Waterstone's Leadership and Culture Advisory Services. Anyone can prompt AI or find a task ripe for automation, fewer have found real problems that merit an AI solution. "AI is meant to be transformational. And yet managing it the ways that they're managing today is not creating the transformation that they're looking for."

sentences.en: Many companies haven't standardized these changes.
sentences.zh: 许多公司尚未对这些变化进行标准化。

sentences.en: A January Deloitte report found that 84% of companies have not redesigned work to meet the capabilities of AI; the emphasis remains on educating workers and pushing them to experiment with AI, rather than altering workflows and career paths to match the tech changes.
sentences.zh: 德勤 1 月份的一份报告发现，84% 的公司没有重新设计工作来满足人工智能的能力；重点仍然是教育工人并推动他们尝试人工智能，而不是改变工作流程和职业道路以适应技术变革。

sentences.en: "Leaders are realizing that this usage conversation isn't having the impact that they were looking for," says Lori Moffatt, managing director of executive recruitment and company culture advisory firm Waterstone's Leadership and Culture Advisory Services.
sentences.zh: 高管招聘和公司文化咨询公司 Waterstone's Leadership and Culture Advisory Services 的董事总经理洛里·莫法特 (Lori Moffatt) 表示：“领导者们意识到，这种使用对话并没有产生他们想要的影响。”

sentences.en: Anyone can prompt AI or find a task ripe for automation, fewer have found real problems that merit an AI solution.
sentences.zh: 任何人都可以推动人工智能或找到适合自动化的任务，但很少有人发现值得人工智能解决方案的真正问题。

sentences.en: "AI is meant to be transformational.
sentences.zh: “人工智能注定是变革性的。

sentences.en: And yet managing it the ways that they're managing today is not creating the transformation that they're looking for."
sentences.zh: 然而，他们今天的管理方式并没有带来他们所寻求的转变。”

blocks.html_en: Marc Cenedella, founder of the career site Ladders, says that while AI advances rapidly, people need more time to fully discover and stretch its technical feats into meaningful work. He encourages workers to experiment with AI, to fail — even if one day we look back and see these early efforts as "goofing around." "It kind of doesn't matter if it's useless or useful at this point," Cenedella says. If AI had obvious benefits, industries would streamline it. "If this was measurable, that would mean it's not an amazing technology."

sentences.en: Marc Cenedella, founder of the career site Ladders, says that while AI advances rapidly, people need more time to fully discover and stretch its technical feats into meaningful work.
sentences.zh: 职业网站 Ladders 的创始人 Marc Cenedella 表示，虽然人工智能发展迅速，但人们需要更多时间来充分发现其技术专长，并将其运用到有意义的工作中。

sentences.en: He encourages workers to experiment with AI, to fail — even if one day we look back and see these early efforts as "goofing around."
sentences.zh: 他鼓励员工尝试人工智能，哪怕失败——即使有一天我们回顾过去，发现这些早期的努力只是“闲逛”。

sentences.en: "It kind of doesn't matter if it's useless or useful at this point," Cenedella says.
sentences.zh: “此时它是无用还是有用并不重要，”塞内德拉说。

sentences.en: If AI had obvious benefits, industries would streamline it.
sentences.zh: 如果人工智能有明显的好处，行业就会简化它。

sentences.en: "If this was measurable, that would mean it's not an amazing technology."
sentences.zh: “如果这是可以测量的，那就意味着这不是一项了不起的技术。”

blocks.html_en: Amanda Hoover is a senior correspondent at Business Insider covering the tech industry. Amanda covers some of the world’s biggest tech companies like Airbnb, Spotify, and Meta and its influential figures. She has written about the evolving workforce, from the ways AI is reshaping roles to how employees are changing their relationship to the job or how they look for work. Her reporting includes deep dives into the tech workforce, looking at the rise of product managers, chief medical officers, and how ageism disproportionately affects tech workers.  Amanda also writes about shifting tech trends, and how people are reevaluating how they spend screen time or what apps they use to meet new people. She has written about the influence of social media platforms like Twitter as well as TikTok trends and YouTube creators.Prior to joining Insider, Amanda covered housing tech and the future of work at WIRED. She has also written for The Star-Ledger, The Boston Globe, and Morning Brew.

content_html_zh:
你擅长人工智能吗？ 你的下一次加薪可能取决于它

Companies are scrambling to figure out how to grade employees' AI use

作者：Amanda Hoover 您目前正在关注该作者！ 想要取消关注吗？ 通过电子邮件中的链接取消订阅。

2026-08-13T08:17:01.234Z

Read in app

世界各地的老板都在忙着弄清楚是否以及如何对员工的人工智能使用进行评分。

在人力资源平台 Gusto，经理们在季度审查期间将员工分为五种人工智能原型之一。 他们可能从“观察者”开始，即那些尚未自己使用人工智能的人。 “集成商”已将人工智能纳入其日常工作的一部分，并因此看到了“持续更好的结果”。 最先进的是“放大器”，他们找到使用人工智能的新方法并与同事分享他们所学到的知识。

Gusto 首席人力官斯科特·赫尔姆斯 (Scott Helmes) 表示，其目的不是用胡萝卜或大棒来统治，而是为了标准化公司实施新兴技术的方式。 “我们希望能够进行一次教练对话，”他告诉我。 下一步是更直接地研究人工智能对员工的影响。 “我认为，这一点的引入确实帮助我们在整个组织内以一致的方式讨论人工智能的流畅性。”

员工人工智能评分标准从 tokenmaxxing 开始，但很快就出现了强烈反对。 亚马逊和优步等公司尝试用排行榜来跟踪人工智能的使用情况，但此后就不再充分利用人工智能。 Duolingo 取消了在员工绩效评估中评估人工智能使用的计划。 Meta 面临下岗工人的诉讼，指控该公司使用人工智能对员工的生产力进行排名，包括他们使用人工智能工具的频率，然后挑选出表现较差的员工进行裁员，而没有将病假和育儿假视为使用率较低的原因。 该公司否认了这些指控。

工作场所无法在人工智能的采用方面取得重大飞跃，除非他们弄清楚微观层面和个体员工办公桌上发生的事情，因为他们聚集了代理和聊天机器人。 试图从超级用户手中剔除那些回避人工智能的人已经越来越成为绩效评估的一部分，但由于许多公司仍在寻求挖掘人工智能的潜力，这可能会让员工努力满足管理者尚未完全形成的期望。 明尼苏达大学工业组织心理学教授理查德·兰德斯（Richard Landers）表示：“有很多人试图以一种不太公平的方式将这一责任推给一线工人。” 他说，一些公司对人工智能的使用进行了错误的奖励，即使它没有实现更好工作的目标。 “你不能真正奖励人工智能的表现，因为我们还不知道它是什么，而且对于不同的工作，它看起来也非常不同。”

人工智能可能是你下一次绩效评估的一个方框。 但当这项技术的成功仍然罕见且主观时，它就成为了一个难以捉摸的类别。

公司在很大程度上放弃了对人工智能系统的订阅和登录，并敦促他们找出如何最好地使用它们。 缺乏培训和强力采用导致了大量工作、安全风险以及混乱的工作流程。 然而，管理者越来越希望评估人们如何使用人工智能。 技术技能培训提供商 General Assembly 在最近对美国和英国 500 名企业领导人进行的一项调查中发现，近一半已将人工智能纳入员工评价中，特别关注人工智能工具使用情况的报告、人工智能带来的绩效改进以及有关效率提高的轶事。

其中大部分都是主观的，与过去的创新不同，过去的创新是公司为特定用例购买软件并对员工进行培训，但有些公司期望由员工领导。

如果没有严格的定量基准，例如花费的代币、生成的代码行、编写的提示和部署的代理，许多人通过跟踪他们所做的事情是否比以前做得更多来评估他们的人工智能使用情况。 软件公司 Typeform 的工程副总裁 Stefan Camilleri 说，他问工程师：“既然我给了你们一个新工具，你们的速度要快多少？” 但仅靠速度并不能解决问题。 “我期待更少的人能做出更雄心勃勃的成果。” 人工智能软件公司 Merge 的联合创始人兼首席执行官丁申思表示，她根据员工使用人工智能的质量来评估他们。 例如，会计人员自动跟踪付款并提高了团队的生产力，丁认为这非常有效。 最高的赞扬来自于那些找到了一个好的用例并将其传递给同事的人。 丁说：“如果你在教其他人，那么这会超出我们的预期水平，而且随着时间的推移，它会对行业产生巨大的影响和复合，人们会因此而真正得到回报。”

对于初创公司来说，他们面临着用更少的人工智能人员做更多事情的压力，但大公司现在也在密切评估员工对人工智能的使用情况。 Meta 去年年底向员工宣布，它将添加“人工智能驱动的影响”作为其绩效评估流程的核心部分。 据报道，埃森哲今年早些时候在考虑员工进行高层晋升时开始监控人工智能登录。 我的同事休·兰利 (Hugh Langley) 今年早些时候报告称，谷歌的非技术员工被告知人工智能的使用可能会出现在他们的绩效评估中。 该公司表示，经理可以在评审中评估人工智能的熟练程度，但这不是必需的。

许多公司仍处于试验阶段，关注人工智能如何增加价值，而不是谁使用最多。 旅行社零售平台 Travelport 的首席转型官 Lee Senderov 表示，她的公司为工程师构建了一个仪表板，使用人工智能来分析代码并确定用于编写代码的工具。 经理可以了解工程师是否没有使用特定的人工智能功能，然后利用这些见解就特定员工理解或不理解的内容以及他们如何编码进行对话。 森德罗夫表示，人工智能针对不同的功能，是根据具体情况而定的，强制推动或推出可能并不适合某些地方。 “我们希望这一切能够通过灵感有机地发生，”她说。

在整个美国企业界，人工智能对绩效评估的实质意义缺乏明确性，导致评估感觉不平衡和不稳定。 《哈佛商业评论》7 月份的一篇文章呼吁审查不要关注产出，而应该关注员工如何评估人工智能的准确性，然后利用判断来覆盖错误，如果员工使用人工智能来提高团队的生产力，以及他们对新技术、政策变化和工作流程的适应程度如何。

许多公司尚未对这些变化进行标准化。 德勤 1 月份的一份报告发现，84% 的公司没有重新设计工作来满足人工智能的能力；重点仍然是教育工人并推动他们尝试人工智能，而不是改变工作流程和职业道路以适应技术变革。 高管招聘和公司文化咨询公司 Waterstone's Leadership and Culture Advisory Services 的董事总经理洛里·莫法特 (Lori Moffatt) 表示：“领导者们意识到，这种使用对话并没有产生他们想要的影响。” 任何人都可以推动人工智能或找到适合自动化的任务，但很少有人发现值得人工智能解决方案的真正问题。 “人工智能注定是变革性的。 然而，他们今天的管理方式并没有带来他们所寻求的转变。”

职业网站 Ladders 的创始人 Marc Cenedella 表示，虽然人工智能发展迅速，但人们需要更多时间来充分发现其技术专长，并将其运用到有意义的工作中。 他鼓励员工尝试人工智能，哪怕失败——即使有一天我们回顾过去，发现这些早期的努力只是“闲逛”。 “此时它是无用还是有用并不重要，”塞内德拉说。 如果人工智能有明显的好处，行业就会简化它。 “如果这是可以测量的，那就意味着这不是一项了不起的技术。”
